about.title: Camarillo Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Camarillo's mix of shopping centers, business parks along Ponderosa Drive, and residential complexes near Santa Rosa Road means falls happen in parking lots, stairwells, and store aisles just like anywhere else. What matters after a fall isn't just that you were hurt, but whether the property owner knew about the hazard, or should have, and failed to fix it or warn you. Wet floors left unmarked, broken pavement, poor lighting, or a torn rug can all become the basis of a claim if the negligence can be shown. Because California law puts the burden on you to prove that notice element, the details you gather right after a fall, photos, witness names, incident reports, matter enormously. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you with an attorney in our network who reviews these cases regularly and works on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters in a Premises Case

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify prior complaints, inspection logs, or patterns that establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Camarillo businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or not looking down, California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover for the share of fault that belongs to the property owner.

items.question: I slipped in a store near the Camarillo Premium Outlets area. What should I do first?
items.answer: Report the fall to management and ask for a written incident report before you leave, and take photos of the exact spot and any warning signs, or absence of them. Get contact information for anyone who saw it happen. These small steps often matter more than people expect once a claim is reviewed.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall, though claims against a government-owned property, such as a public sidewalk or building, involve a much shorter deadline to file a claim. It's worth having a case reviewed sooner rather than later so evidence isn't lost.

items.question: Will it hurt my case if I wasn't paying attention when I fell?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California uses a pure comparative fault system, so even if you're found partially responsible, you can still recover a reduced amount tied to the property owner's share of fault. An attorney can walk through how that might apply to your specific situation.
